findings.summary: The second YAML block mixes the Pod's volumes with a container-level volumeMounts line behind a comment, so it isn't a valid fragment.
findings.evidence:
# in the container:
volumeMounts: [{name: d, mountPath: /data}]
findings.fix: Show a minimal Pod spec with volumes at the Pod level and volumeMounts nested under the container.

findings.summary: One gotcha bullet holds two ideas: PVCs are kept on scale-down or delete, and how to clean them up.
findings.evidence: Scale-down or delete keeps PVCs: clean up by hand or set persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy
findings.fix: Split it into 'Scale-down or delete keeps PVCs' and 'Clean up by hand or set persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy'.

findings.summary: The CronJob to Job to Pods relationship is a bare list of labels, so the flow can't be followed as a diagram.
findings.evidence: CronJob / cron schedule / Job / runs to completion / Pods / retried on failure
findings.fix: Draw it as a chain: CronJob (schedule) -> Job (runs to completion) -> Pods (retried on failure).

findings.summary: The 'Quick map' table mixes a command row into a table of setting values.
findings.evidence: Setting | Values ... kubectl get ds | per-node DaemonSet coverage
findings.fix: Remove the kubectl get ds row from the table and add it to a bash block, for example the one in section 2, with a one-line note.
